items.title: The Second Branch: Genuine Teaching Requires Both a Good Teacher and a Good Listener

items.zh: 云何聞正法圓滿？謂若正說法，若正聞法，二種總名聞正法圓滿。
items.en: What is complete access to hearing the true teaching? Both correct teaching and correct listening together are called complete access to hearing the true teaching.

items.zh: 又正說法略有二種。所謂隨順及無染污。廣說當知有二十種。如菩薩地當說。又正聞法略有四種。一、遠離憍傲；二、遠離輕蔑，三、遠離怯弱，四、遠離散亂。遠離如是四種過失而聽法者，名正聞法。當知廣說有十六種，亦如菩薩地中當說。

items.title: The Third Branch: Ten Stages From First Hearing to Final Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 云何涅槃為上首？謂如來弟子依生圓滿轉時，如先所說相而聽聞正法，唯以涅槃而為上首。唯求涅槃、唯緣涅槃而聽聞法，不為引他令信於己，不為利養恭敬稱譽。
items.en: What is nirvāṇa held as the governing aim? It means that when the Tathāgata's disciples, resting on a favourable rebirth-basis, listen to the true teaching in the manner already described, they hold nirvāṇa alone as the governing aim — seeking nirvāṇa alone, listening with nirvāṇa alone in mind, never to win others' trust in themselves, and never for material gain, honour, or praise.

items.zh: 又緣涅槃而聽法者，有十法轉，涅槃為首。謂依止有餘依涅槃界，及無餘依涅槃界。當知依止有餘依涅槃界，有九法轉，涅槃為首；依止無餘依涅槃界，有一法轉，涅槃為首。謂以聞所成慧為因，於道、道果涅槃，起三種信解。一、信實有性，二、信有功德，三、信己有能得樂方便。如是信解生已，為欲成辦思所成智，身心遠離憒鬧而住，遠離障蓋諸惡尋思。依止此故，便能趣入善決定義思所成智。依止此故，又能趣入無間、殷重二修方便。由此次第，乃至證得修所成智。依止此故，見生死過失、發起勝解；見涅槃功德，發起勝解。由串修故，入諦現觀，先得見道有學解脫。已得見迹，於上修道由數習故，更復證得無學解脫。由證此故，解脫圓滿。即此解脫圓滿，名有餘依涅槃界。即此涅槃以為上首，令前九法次第修習而得圓滿。當知即此解脫圓滿，以無餘依涅槃界而為上首。如是涅槃為首聽聞正法，當知獲得五種勝利。何等為五？

items.title: The Third Branch Closes: Five Benefits of Keeping Nirvāṇa in View

items.zh: 謂聽聞法時，饒益自他；修正行時，饒益自他；及能證得眾苦邊際。
items.en: Namely: benefiting both self and other while listening to the teaching; benefiting both self and other while cultivating right practice; and being able to reach the very limit of suffering.

items.zh: 若說法師，為此義故宣說正法，其聽法者，即以此意而聽正法；是故此時名饒益他。又以善心聽聞正法，便能領受所說法義甚深上味，因此證得廣大歡喜，又能引發出離善根；是故此時能自饒益。若有正修法隨法行大師，為欲建立正法，方便示現成正等覺，云何令彼正修行轉；故彼修習正法行時，即是法爾供養大師。是故說此名饒益他。因此正行，堪能證得寂靜清涼，唯有餘依涅槃之界；是故說此能自饒益。若無餘依涅槃界中般涅槃時，名為證得眾苦邊際。是名涅槃以為上首，聽聞正法所得勝利。如是名為涅槃為首所有廣義。除此更無若過若增。云何能熟解脫慧之成熟？謂毘鉢舍那支成熟故，亦名慧成熟；奢摩他支成熟故，亦名慧成熟。

items.title: The Fourth Branch: Ten Steps That Ripen Calm-Abiding and Insight Into Genuine Liberation

items.zh: 所以者何？定心中慧，於所知境清淨轉故。
items.en: Why is this so? Because it is precisely the wisdom present within a concentrated mind that operates purely with regard to what is known.

blocks.text: Branches two to four. The second describes right teaching and right listening; the third, how keeping nirvāṇa as the aim shapes everything; the fourth, how calm and insight ripen into liberating wisdom. A few passages are untranslated.

"Both correct teaching and correct listening together are called complete access to hearing the true teaching." The teacher speaks in accord with the noble path, not from their own ideas and not for gain. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you hope for fame and gain, what you say "can no longer be called the true Dharma". The listener listens with respect, without pride (Master Cháng Bǎi: "on the high mountain of pride, the water of Dharma cannot enter") and without faint-heartedness, thinking "this is too high for me".
One listens "seeking nirvāṇa alone", not to win others' trust or for gain. Venerable Miào Jìng: seeking nirvāṇa is the fruit; keeping it in mind is the cause.

The untranslated prose (0389a24) describes ten steps headed by nirvāṇa: from wisdom born of hearing comes threefold faith in the path and its fruit (that they are real, that they have value, that one can attain them); then solitude and freedom from hindrances; wisdom from reflection; continuous and earnest practice; wisdom from cultivation; seeing the faults of saṃsāra and the merits of nirvāṇa; entry into the truths; the trainee's liberation; and liberation beyond training, which is nirvāṇa with remainder. The tenth is nirvāṇa without remainder.

Listening this way benefits both teacher and listener; brings deep joy; is an offering to the Buddha, who awakened in order that the Dharma be practised; leads to the coolness of nirvāṇa with remainder; and finally to the end of all suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng: the trainee's liberation is "stillness"; the arhat's, "coolness".

Wisdom ripens when both the **insight** factor and the **calm** factor ripen. Venerable Miào Jìng raises the obvious question: calm is concentration, so how can it be "wisdom"? Because calm is the condition that lets insight become liberating. Master Cháng Bǎi cites the *Tattvasiddhi*: if wisdom is strong, even a moment of concentration can cut affliction.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call "complete access to hearing the true teaching"?
options: correct teaching and correct listening together
quiz.why: "Both correct teaching and correct listening together are called complete access to hearing the true teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: if what is taught is not the true Dharma, or the listening is faulty, hearing is not complete.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the teacher being "undefiled"?
options: seeking fame and gain makes one impure, and what one says is affected — it cannot be called the true Dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if you hope for fame and gain, you are impure, and what you say is affected — it can no longer be called the true Dharma.

quiz.q: Why should one not be proud when listening, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the high mountain of pride lets no Dharma water in
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: on the high mountain of pride, the water of Dharma cannot enter — so one should not feel proud.

quiz.q: A correct listener should not be "faint-hearted." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: thinking "this is too high, I can't learn it" is faint-heartedness; Cháng Bǎi: whoever strives can do it — the Buddha too was once an ordinary being
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: thinking "this Dharma is too high; I can't do it, I can't learn it" — that is faint-heartedness. Master Cháng Bǎi: whoever strives can be like him; the Buddha too became a buddha from an ordinary being.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "seeking nirvāṇa alone" from "keeping nirvāṇa alone in mind"?
options: seeking is the fruit; keeping in mind is the cause of attaining it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "seeking nirvāṇa alone" is the fruit; "keeping nirvāṇa alone in mind" is cultivating the cause — the cause of attaining nirvāṇa is called "keeping it in mind."

quiz.q: What do the two masters call the liberation of trainees and of those beyond training?
options: the trainee's liberation is "stillness," the arhat's is "coolness"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the trainee's liberation is called stillness; the liberation of one beyond training is called coolness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the trainee's liberation means no more rebirth in the lower realms; the arhat, having cut all craving and view afflictions of the three realms, is called cool.

quiz.q: The treatise says "the wisdom within a concentrated mind operates purely." What difficulty does Venerable Miào Jìng raise, and how does he resolve it?
options: calm is concentration — how can it be wisdom? Because concentration helps wisdom see reality, it too is called wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: calm-abiding is concentration, and when successful it is still concentration — how can it be called wisdom? This is a difficult point. Then: this "wisdom in the concentrated mind" — since concentration helps wisdom see the true nature of things, concentration is also called wisdom.
